integration_requests.action: Install the complete dynamic backend files, then apply openvpn_session after connected_vpn_nullable and openvpn_lifecycle. Add its apply.sh to the aggregate preparation without editing public IPC signatures. Earlier exact guards recognize only this full exact follow-up.

Rebuild locked OpenVPN with the expanded existing 0001 port patch; its new dns.c/dns.h/tun_afunix.c changes export final negotiated DNS before AF_UNIX bridge fork. Old dependency receipts/binaries must not be reused.

Compile/link the final actual controller/service/base/supervisor/bridge translation units for all three target architectures. Verify process /proc/exe and PPid read permission under the actual NetworkVpnService identity; add only a demonstrated narrow policy if needed. startup.service.ctl read access was already verified by parent and does not need expansion.

Run all three test_batch_network_* modules in private Linux scratch with the frozen recipe/source snapshot. In particular run test_linux_parent_death_kills_real_exec_child and test_sigkill_stale_secret_cleanup_no_symlink_or_unknown_tree_traversal. Keep fixed source/out mounts read-only.

Keep the first-new-package gate: a real TLS peer must exercise dual-stack addresses, negotiated DNS and routes, data/endpoint bypass, forced reconnect with new DNS/routes, start/stop failure, abrupt init SIGKILL/restart, invalid/stale generation, real caller PID/lineage, permission and account boundaries before remaining five packages.
Finish external callback epoch/account/generation snapshots and unregister/death/teardown/reentry tests as an independent batch. No incomplete async callback code is included here.

Implement/validate the API26 Bluetooth four-argument startPairOutOfBand parser/export and genuine backend/peer work; coordinate BPF/kernel, USB MTP provider and bridge/tap topology with their central owners.

arkts_export:@ohos.bluetooth.connection:.finding: Fixed NAPI registers pairDeviceOutOfBand only. API 26 startPairOutOfBand adds a deviceId parameter and optional P192/P256 data, so aliasing the existing three-argument parser is incorrect.
remaining: Implement and boundary-test the API 26 four-argument parser/export while preserving native permission checks.
Provide an actual Bluetooth controller/vendor transport and OOB-capable peer; verify pairing events, errors and cleanup.

behavior:netmanager-ebpf-backend.finding: The repository already has BPF_SYSCALL/CGROUP_BPF kernel candidates for all three architectures. Historical ENOSYS alone cannot establish the behavior of the next rebuilt kernel, and candidate configuration does not prove UID policy/statistics.
remaining: Boot a newly packaged kernel and verify actual BPF program/map loading and attachment, UID accounting, access-policy enforcement, denied caller boundaries and cleanup.
Kernel/defconfig modifications belong to central integration; this batch did not edit them.

behavior:bluetooth-state-transition-fals.finding: Historical adapter/vendor-loader rollback remains open. Existing enum/export repairs cannot substitute for a Bluetooth transport or confirm adapter state transitions.
remaining: Select a real virtual or passthrough controller and matching vendor/HDI transport.
Use a new package and peer to verify enable/disable final state, pairing/data, unplug and cleanup; request acceptance must not count as enabled.

behavior:wifi-sta-backend-unavailable.finding: The repository already stages mac80211_hwsim/virt_wifi modules and WPA scan/channel/software-PNO/regulatory candidates. Their own evidence explicitly leaves AP association/data/P2P validation open; historical absent-module evidence must not be misreported as a fresh-source result.
remaining: Validate the actual packaged modules, service identity, real radio interface and regulatory behavior.
Run STA/AP association, DHCP, packet transfer, P2P, failure, device-change and teardown tests using a genuine compatible peer.

behavior:usb-manager-device-query.finding: Host enumeration and a USB service alone do not establish gadget/device-mode operation. The historical missing UDC/configfs binding and MTP service declaration mismatch remain separate unresolved dependencies.
remaining: Provide actual QEMU host-device fixtures/passthrough and a genuine UDC backend for device mode.
Coordinate MtpService HAP/provider declaration with the owning app/media group through the parent; do not edit their files.
Validate descriptor/query/open/permission/data/unplug/cleanup behavior and real MTP activation on a new package.

behavior:peer-device-user-nat-isolation.finding: The current package launcher still generates a user-mode NAT netdev, preventing ordinary peer discovery between independent guests. Correcting a single service implementation cannot create a shared layer-2 test network.
remaining: Parent owns shared launcher changes: design explicit bridge/tap networking with unique interfaces, MACs, ports and two independent device identities.
Validate discovery, account/authentication boundaries, distributed/cast data and peer removal with two newly packaged guests.

arkts_export:@ohos.net.vpn:getConnectedS.finding: Second source batch atomically binds configuration/password/kernel-random generation to the actual native supervisor IPC PID; late events resolve that exact controller and real bridge lineage. Full checked negotiated address/route/DNS snapshots replace old data. Reconnect requires fresh bridge/TLS; one-supervisor second-owner requests reject before disrupting the first. SIGKILL-stale private session files prune under an exclusive no-follow owned root. No complete VPN claim.
remaining: Final cross-architecture full-TU compilation/linking and actual Linux/native PID/lineage checks.
Complete external callback cancellation/epoch/account/generation and reentry handling.

Simultaneous OpenVPN owners need a real broker; current second owner rejects honestly. persist-tun configuration-update channel, split/encrypted DNS policies and nonzero route metric mapping remain unsupported.
First-new-package real TLS peer, DNS/IPv6/routes/data/endpoint bypass, reconnect, SIGKILL/restart, teardown, permissions and account/owner boundaries.
